text: Git branching is an important part of a version control workflow. When developers work on new features, they create feature branches, which allow them to make changes without affecting the main codebase. This keeps the main branch stable and safe. Once the work is finished, the branch is merged back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often use pull requests to review the code together. This process helps catch mistakes early and improves code quality. By using branches, teams can work on different tasks at the same time without conflicts. Overall, understanding branching makes collaboration smoother and keeps projects organized.
